bullets: How a plant grows from a seed and makes new seeds, and how a butterfly grows from an egg - two cycles that never stop
slides.heading: Life cycles: plants and animals
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we follow two life cycles - a seed that wakes up, sprouts and grows into a flowering plant that makes new seeds, and an egg that hatches into a caterpillar and changes into a butterfly.

bullets: Follow a seed as it sprouts, grows and flowers, then makes new seeds
Follow an egg as it hatches into a caterpillar, rests as a pupa and emerges as a butterfly
Explain why the flower is not the end of the life of the plant
slides.heading: What we will learn
slides.notes: Read the three goals aloud and tell the class: keep these in mind, because the exit ticket at the end will ask you to put both cycles in order and spot the mistake about the flower being the end.

bullets: A pupil says the flower is the end of the life of the plant, because it is the last part to appear
Is the flower really the finish, or does something new start inside it?
slides.heading: Is the flower the end of the plant?
slides.notes: Pose the claim from scene s2 without the verdict first: ask for a show of hands on whether the flower is the end of the plant, take two or three answers without judging them, and say scene s2 settles this exactly.

bullets: A life cycle is the circle of changes a living thing goes through as it grows
The cycle never just stops: the adult makes new young, and the circle starts again
slides.heading: A life cycle goes round and round
slides.notes: Say this slowly, because it is the big idea of the whole lesson: plants and animals grow and change in a circle - seed to plant to new seeds, egg to caterpillar to butterfly to new eggs.

bullets: A seed rests in the soil until water, warmth and light wake it up
The seed sprouts: a root grows down and a green shoot grows up into a seedling
slides.heading: A seed wakes up and sprouts
slides.notes: Narrate the seed waking up in the soil, watch the first root grow down and the shoot push up, and name the baby plant that appears: a seedling.

bullets: The seedling grows into an adult plant and opens a big, showy flower
Inside the flower, new seeds are forming - so the flower starts the next round instead of ending the cycle
slides.heading: Watch out: the flower is not the end of the plant
slides.notes: Hold the mistake up first - the flower looks like the finish because it is the biggest, showiest and last part to appear - then look inside the flower and watch the new seeds forming, which proves the cycle starts again.

bullets: A butterfly lays tiny eggs on a leaf
Each egg hatches into a caterpillar, which munches leaves and grows bigger
slides.heading: An egg hatches into a caterpillar
slides.notes: Watch the tiny eggs on the leaf, then follow one egg as it hatches: out comes a caterpillar, the growing-up stage of the butterfly, and it eats and grows.

bullets: The caterpillar rests inside a pupa while its body changes
An adult butterfly comes out, ready to lay eggs so the cycle repeats
slides.heading: The butterfly emerges and the cycle repeats
slides.notes: Follow the caterpillar into its pupa, wait while the body changes inside, then watch the adult butterfly emerge - and point out it will lay eggs, so the whole cycle starts again.

bullets: Start with one seed: it sprouts into a seedling, grows into a flowering plant, and its flower makes new seeds
Each stop is a state change: seed, seedling, adult plant, flower, new seeds
slides.heading: Worked example: follow one seed all the way round
slides.notes: Talk through scenes s1 and s2 slowly and name each change of state: the seed wakes and sprouts, the seedling grows up and flowers, and inside the flower the next seeds are already forming.

bullets: Put the plant cycle in order: seed, seedling, adult plant, flower - then what comes next?
Explain to your partner why the flower is not the end, using the words new seeds in your answer
slides.heading: Your turn: put both cycles in order
slides.notes: Give pairs three minutes, then cold-call one pair on each cycle: press them to end the plant cycle with new seeds forming inside the flower, not with the flower itself.

bullets: On your own: draw the butterfly cycle and label egg, caterpillar, pupa and adult butterfly
Explain in one sentence why the flower is not the end of the life of the plant
slides.heading: Exit ticket: show what you know
slides.notes: Collect these before anyone leaves and say: I am looking for all four butterfly stages labelled in order, plus one clear sentence about new seeds forming inside the flower.
